summary: Preinstall dropper executes obfuscated Bun-compiled payload while impersonating @verdocs/web-sdk-react
details: The package's `preinstall` lifecycle hook runs an obfuscated `setup.mjs` (hex-named `_0xXXXX` identifiers) that downloads a Bun runtime tarball from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases`, extracts it to a temp directory, sets it executable, and uses that freshly-fetched alternate runtime to execute the bundled 720KB `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) with a string-array + rotate/shuffle deobfuscator (`WV8StW`), hex-named identifiers, and a large constants table (`n7gIxM`); its contents are not humanly readable and are not reconcilable with the stated purpose of a React signing SDK. Using an alien runtime to execute the bundled opaque payload evades inspection by Node-based tooling. The package additionally impersonates the legitimate `@verdocs/web-sdk-react`: `package.json` description is "Verdocs Web SDK for React" and the README is a verbatim copy of the Verdocs SDK README (instructing users to `npm i -S @verdocs/web-sdk-react`), while the actual package is published under the unrelated `@hubsync` scope. The deceptive naming is the entry vector for the install-time execution of the obfuscated Bun payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
